recipes.dish: Sage Chicken Cutlets with Apple-Onion Pan Juices
recipes.story_source: NorthStar original culinary working recipe; primary sources inform handling and individualized dietary planning
recipes.rights_status: NorthStar original recipe text and AI illustration; no third-party recipe or image reproduced
recipes.yield: 4 servings; one cutlet and one-quarter of fruit and onion each
ingredients: 1 pound (454 g) boneless skinless chicken breast, divided into four cutlets about 1/2 inch thick
1 medium apple (about 180 g), cored and thinly sliced
instructions: Read the chicken label for added solution or phosphate ingredients; keep it refrigerated while preparing produce.
Wash apple and sage under running water, then slice the apple and peeled onion on a clean produce board.
Prepare four evenly thick cutlets on a separate raw-poultry surface; wash hands and clean the surface and tools after use.
Heat half the oil in a large skillet over medium heat; add onion and cook for 4 minutes.
Add apple slices and cook for 3 minutes, then transfer fruit and onion to a clean bowl.
Add remaining oil to the skillet; season cutlets with pepper and cook for 3-4 minutes per side.
Return apple and onion to the skillet; add sage, water and vinegar and bring to a simmer.
Simmer for 3-5 minutes or longer as needed; check every cutlet reaches 165 F (74 C) in its thickest part with a clean thermometer.
Use clean serving utensils to divide into four portions, spooning the apple-onion pan juices over each cutlet.
Chill leftovers promptly in shallow containers and follow the storage note.

recipes.dish: Parsley Turkey Patties with Cucumber Ribbons
recipes.story_source: NorthStar original culinary working recipe; primary sources inform handling and individualized dietary planning
recipes.rights_status: NorthStar original recipe text and AI illustration; no third-party recipe or image reproduced
recipes.yield: 4 servings; two small patties and one-quarter of cucumber each
instructions: Read turkey and breadcrumb labels for added salt, phosphates and allergens. Keep turkey and egg refrigerated until mixing.
Wash cucumber, parsley and lemon under running water; shave cucumber into ribbons with a peeler, stopping at the watery seed core.
Toss ribbons with lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of the oil; cover and refrigerate while cooking the patties.
In a bowl combine turkey, pasteurized egg, breadcrumbs, parsley, garlic and pepper without overworking; do not taste the raw mixture.
Shape into eight equal patties about 2 1/2 inches across and 1/2 inch thick; wash hands and clean raw-poultry tools.
Warm the remaining 2 teaspoons oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat; add patties in a single layer, working in batches if needed.
Cook for 5-6 minutes per side, reducing heat if they brown too quickly.
Check every patty reaches 165 F (74 C) in the center, inserting a clean thermometer sideways; continue cooking as needed.
Serve two patties per person with one-quarter of the cold cucumber ribbons, using clean utensils.
Refrigerate remaining patties and cucumber separately and follow the storage note.

ingredients: 1 pound (454 g) haddock, divided into four fillets, thawed in the refrigerator if frozen
instructions: Heat the oven to 425 F (218 C). Read fish labels for added solutions or phosphate ingredients.
Wash cauliflower, lemon and parsley under running water; cut florets into roughly one-inch pieces.
Toss cauliflower with 2 teaspoons oil and half the pepper on a rimmed baking sheet.
Roast for 12 minutes, then turn the florets with a spatula.
On a separate raw-fish surface, arrange chilled haddock in a small baking dish; wash hands after handling.

Put the fish dish in the oven alongside the cauliflower; bake for 12-16 minutes, adjusting for fillet thickness.
Verify every fillet reaches 145 F (63 C) with a clean thermometer; continue roasting cauliflower until tender with browned edges.
Divide fish and cauliflower among four plates; finish with the measured lemon juice, zest and parsley.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly and follow the storage note.

recipes.dish: Ginger Pork Tenderloin with Warm Pear Slices
recipes.story_source: NorthStar original culinary working recipe; primary sources inform handling and individualized dietary planning
recipes.rights_status: NorthStar original recipe text and AI illustration; no third-party recipe or image reproduced
recipes.yield: 4 servings; one-quarter of sliced tenderloin and pear each
recipes.time: 15 minutes prep + 25-35 minutes roasting + at least 3 minutes rest; pears cook during roasting
ingredients: 1 small whole pork tenderloin, about 1 pound (454 g), unseasoned
1 medium firm pear (about 180 g), cored and sliced
instructions: Heat the oven to 400 F (204 C). Check the pork label for brine, added salt or phosphate ingredients.
Wash pear and ginger under running water; slice pear and grate peeled ginger using clean produce tools.
Keep pork whole for a reliable center-temperature check; place it in a small roasting pan on a separate raw-meat surface.
Rub pork with 2 teaspoons oil, half the ginger and pepper; wash hands and clean raw-meat tools.
Roast for 25-35 minutes, beginning temperature checks at 20 minutes because size and ovens vary.
Meanwhile warm the remaining teaspoon oil in a skillet; cook pear slices over medium heat for 4 minutes.
Add remaining ginger, rice vinegar and water to the pears; simmer for 2-3 minutes until just tender.
Check the thickest center of the whole tenderloin reaches at least 145 F (63 C), then rest it for at least 3 minutes before cutting.
Using a clean board and knife, slice the rested pork and divide into four portions with warm pears and their juices.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers and follow the storage note.

recipes.yield: 4 side servings; one-quarter of polenta and peppers each
recipes.time: 15 minutes prep + 30-40 minutes cooking, with overlapping steps
ingredients: 1/2 cup (80 g) ordinary yellow cornmeal, not instant
2 cups water, plus up to 1/4 cup hot water only if needed
1 medium red bell pepper, cut into strips
instructions: Read the cornmeal label for allergens and preparation directions; heat the oven to 425 F (218 C).
Wash pepper and scallions under running water; remove pepper seeds and cut it into thin strips.
Toss pepper strips with 1 teaspoon oil on a rimmed baking sheet.
Roast for 18-22 minutes, turning once, until soft and lightly browned at the edges.
Meanwhile bring 2 cups water to a gentle boil in a heavy saucepan.
Whisk in cornmeal slowly, then reduce heat to low; stir frequently to prevent lumps and sticking.
Cook for 25-35 minutes or the package-directed time until smooth and tender; add a little of the optional hot water only if too thick.
Stir remaining 2 teaspoons oil and pepper into polenta; fold half the scallions into the roasted pepper strips.
Divide polenta among four small bowls; top each with one-quarter of peppers and the remaining scallions.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly in shallow containers and follow the storage note.

recipes.time: 15 minutes prep + 8 minutes skillet cooking + 20-28 minutes baking + 5 minutes rest
instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F (177 C). Read egg and milk labels; grease an 8-inch-square dish with 1 teaspoon oil.
Wash zucchini and dill under running water, then grate zucchini and dice peeled onion on a clean board.
Warm the remaining teaspoon oil in a skillet over medium heat; cook onion for 3 minutes.
Add zucchini and cook for 5 minutes, stirring until visible liquid mostly evaporates.
Spread vegetables in the baking dish and let them cool briefly while mixing the eggs.

Pour egg mixture over the vegetables and distribute them evenly with a clean fork.
Bake for 20-28 minutes until the center reaches 165 F (74 C) with a clean thermometer and no liquid egg remains.
Rest for 5 minutes, then cut into four equal squares and serve one per person.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly and follow the storage note.

ingredients: 1 cup cooked white rice, promptly chilled after cooking and kept refrigerated
1 cup (about 150 g) hulled fresh strawberries, cut into small pieces
1 teaspoon olive oil for the ramekins
instructions: Use rice with a known safe refrigeration history and within its storage period; discard rice with uncertain time or temperature history.
Heat the oven to 350 F (177 C); grease four oven-safe 6-ounce ramekins with the measured oil and place them on a baking tray.
Wash strawberries under running water before hulling and cutting into small pieces.
Break up chilled rice with a fork and divide it equally among the ramekins.
Divide strawberry pieces among the cups and gently mix with the rice.
Whisk pasteurized egg, milk, sugar and vanilla in a clean bowl; do not taste the uncooked custard.
Divide the custard evenly among the four ramekins and stir each gently to distribute it.
Bake for 25-35 minutes, checking each center reaches 165 F (74 C) and custard is set; continue as needed.
Let stand for 10 minutes before serving one warm cup per person; ramekins remain hot.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly and follow the storage note.

recipes.time: 20 minutes prep + 7 minutes filling cooking + 15 minutes cooling + 18-22 minutes baking + 5 minutes rest; phyllo thawing additional
ingredients: 4 rectangular phyllo sheets, about 9 by 14 inches each, thawed in the refrigerator according to the package
1 medium apple (about 180 g), peeled, cored and finely diced
instructions: Thaw phyllo according to its package and keep it covered to prevent drying; read its allergen and sodium information.
Wash apple and lemon under running water before peeling, coring and finely dicing the apple.
Combine apple, sugar, cinnamon, lemon juice and water in a small skillet over medium heat.
Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring until apple softens and most liquid evaporates; spread in a shallow dish and cool for about 15 minutes.
Heat the oven to 375 F (191 C) and line a baking tray with parchment.
Lay out one phyllo sheet, brush lightly with some measured oil, then fold lengthwise into thirds to make a long strip.
Place one-quarter of the cooled filling near one end; fold a corner over it to form a triangle, continuing triangular folds to the end.
Repeat with the remaining sheets and filling; brush pocket tops lightly with the remaining oil.
Bake for 18-22 minutes or the package-directed bake until layers are crisp and golden; do not taste uncooked pastry.
Rest for 5 minutes before serving one pocket each; refrigerate leftovers promptly and follow the storage note.
recipes.history_fact: Original NorthStar formulation, not kitchen-tested. The cited agencies support handling and planning notes; they do not endorse or test this recipe.

recipes.yield: 6 servings; two cookies each from twelve
recipes.time: 15 minutes prep + 14-18 minutes baking + 15 minutes cooling
ingredients: 3 tablespoons (43 g) unsalted butter made from pasteurized milk, softened
instructions: Heat the oven to 350 F (177 C) and line a baking sheet with parchment; read flour, oats, butter and baking-powder labels.
Wash blueberries and lemon under running water; dry berries gently and grate the measured zest.
Mix flour, rolled oats and baking powder in a bowl.
In a second bowl beat softened butter and sugar until creamy, about 2 minutes.
Beat in pasteurized egg, vanilla and lemon zest until combined.
Stir dry ingredients into the wet mixture, then fold in blueberries gently; do not taste the raw dough.
Drop twelve equal mounds on the baking sheet with at least 2 inches between them; flatten slightly with a spoon.
Bake for 14-18 minutes until edges are golden, tops are set and centers have no wet dough; rotate the tray if needed.
Cool on the tray for 5 minutes, then move to a rack for 10 minutes; serve two cookies per portion.
Once fully cool, pack extras in a covered container; refrigerate and use within 3-4 days for a conservative home-storage plan, or freeze in a labeled airtight container.
